title: Understanding Your Paycheck & Pay Stub
summary: Learn how a paycheck and pay stub describe your work, earnings, pay period, hours or salary information, deductions, and take-home pay.
objectives: Identify common sections of a pay stub.
Recognize when paycheck information should be reviewed or clarified.

vocab.def: The span of time for which an employer calculates an employee's pay.
Pay attributed to work during a pay period before applicable deductions are considered.
An amount subtracted from pay for an applicable tax, benefit, contribution, or other authorized purpose.
The amount remaining after applicable deductions are subtracted from earnings.

sections.heading: A paycheck tells only part of the story
sections.body: The amount deposited or paid to you is usually accompanied by a pay statement or pay stub. That statement helps explain how the final amount was calculated.

sections.heading: Start with the pay period
sections.body: A pay stub normally identifies the dates covered by the payment. Depending on the job, earnings may be based on hours worked, salary, overtime, commissions, bonuses, tips, or other compensation arrangements.

sections.heading: Earnings and net pay are different
sections.body: The amount earned before applicable deductions is not always the same as the amount received. Understanding that difference is an important part of planning around a job.

sections.heading: Review information instead of assuming it is correct
sections.body: Check that the pay period, hours or salary information, earnings, deductions, and final pay make sense. If something appears unclear, use the employer's appropriate payroll, supervisor, or human-resources process to ask for clarification.

practice.prompt: A pay stub shows $600 in earnings and $510 in net pay. Does that automatically mean $90 disappeared?
practice.answer: No. Review the listed deductions to understand how the net-pay amount was calculated.

practice.prompt: Your pay stub appears to show fewer hours than you expected. What is the responsible next step?
practice.answer: Review your own records and use the employer's appropriate process to ask for clarification.

quiz.question: What is net pay?
options: The amount remaining after applicable deductions are subtracted
Always the same amount as gross earnings
The amount an employer advertises as an annual salary
A credit score connected to employment
quiz.answer: The amount remaining after applicable deductions are subtracted

lab.objective: Review a simulated pay stub and identify the pay period, earnings, deductions, and net pay without using real learner financial information.

reflectionPrompt: Why is it important to understand how the amount you earned relates to the amount you actually receive?
